findings.message: At the default batch of 16 the noise is only 7.5%, so the purple Next step arrow and the dark Full-batch step arrow almost completely overlap. Their two labels point at nearly the same tip, so the stochastic difference is hard to see in the opening view. A small sideways offset, or a default where the gap is visible, would help.

The batch size control and the 'New run, keep old path' action were not sampled. The SGD-specific behaviour (noisier steps at batch 1 or 4, no noise at 256) and the kept path cannot be confirmed from these captures.

The noise is modelled as a share of the slope, so it fades to nothing at the lowest point. Real SGD with a fixed rate keeps jittering around the minimum. The assumptions disclose this, but stating it more prominently would keep learners from thinking SGD settles exactly. Loss 0.034 after 14 steps matches the formula (z shrinks by 0.874 each step).
Both arrows are hidden here because the step times 5 is shorter than the 0.4 cutoff (disclosed). Near the lowest point the learner loses the step cue entirely.

The host-drawn trail tube appears twisted and thin on some segments of the zigzag, which makes the path look uneven. The step points themselves (x grows by a factor of -1.8 each step, giving 3.36 after 6 steps, and loss 8.011) are correct.
